steps.tx: **Brainstem death** is a known irreversible cause, a deep coma, exclusion of confounders, absent brainstem reflexes, and an apnoea test. The patient is warmed to at least 36 C, sedatives have cleared, and the sodium and the glucose are not extreme. A cold patient, or a patient still full of sedative, is not ready for the examination. A temperature below 36 C is not an acceptable test condition.

vis.alt: Absent pupil, corneal, cold-water oculovestibular, and gag reflexes.
vis.caption: Fixed pupils, an absent corneal reflex, no eye movement to cold water, and an absent gag. These are brainstem reflexes. The drawing is not the apnoea test and it does not show a temperature of 36 C. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: The **apnoea test** is started from a PaCO2 near 40 mmHg. The patient is preoxygenated and then disconnected. The test is support for brain death when there is no breath and the PaCO2 is at least 60 mmHg, or it has risen by at least 20 mmHg. A hypoxic patient is not pushed through a failed disconnection. The test is aborted if the oxygen falls.

vis.alt: Coronal drawing of mass effect with midline shift and herniation.
vis.caption: Structural mass effect and herniation, a cause that can reach the brainstem. This is not the apnoea test. PaCO2 of 40, 60, or a rise of 20 is not drawn. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Indian rules are two examinations by doctors who are not the transplant retrieval team, separated by at least **6 hours** in adults. The form is the legal record. One examination is not enough. The retrieving surgeons are not the doctors who certify the death.

steps.tx: **Ancillary tests**, four-vessel angiography, a radionuclide scan, or an EEG, are used only when a clinical part cannot be completed, such as an apnoea test that failed from hypoxia. They are not a shortcut past an unfinished examination. A scan is not a replacement for reflexes that were never tested.

left.title: When an ancillary test is used
points: A clinical part cannot be finished
The rest of the exam is still done

steps.tx: **Spinal reflexes**, including the Lazarus sign, can persist, and they do not exclude brain death. They are explained to the family before they are misread as life. A limb that moves is not a brainstem. The movement is a spinal cord that is still capable of a reflex.

steps.tx: A **vegetative state** and brain death are not the same condition. A vegetative state has a sleep-wake cycle and brainstem function. Brain death has neither. The family is not told that the two labels are interchangeable, because the prognosis and the law are different.

right.title: Brain death
points: The certificate is a different act

steps.tx: After consent, donor care is lung-protective ventilation, treatment of **diabetes insipidus** with **vasopressin**, and replacement of cortisol. The goal is organ perfusion, and it is not a new diagnosis to chase for its own sake. A rising sodium with a large urine output is diabetes insipidus until it is treated. Vasopressin is for that water loss, and it is also a vasopressor.

steps.tx: The family conversation about **donation** is separated from the declaration of death. The certifying doctors are not the retrieving surgeons. The two conversations are not folded into one visit. A declaration is complete before donation is discussed, so the certificate is not felt as a request for organs.
